# Steam turbine (`steam_turbine`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/energy.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Energy & engines (`energy`)
- Deps: needs safety_valve_boiler, machine_tools; helped by high_pressure_steam, separate_condenser, bessemer_steel, dynamo_electric_motor, water_turbine
- Core idea: Steam expanding through a nozzle leaves at around 1,000 m per second, and a wheel takes the most from a jet when its blades move at about half the jet's speed, which would tear any single wheel apart. Two ways out: one small wheel of the best steel at 30,000 turns a minute with reduction gearing (de Laval), or let the pressure fall in many small steps through alternating rings of fixed and moving blades along a drum, each step giving only a modest steam speed (Parsons). There is no reciprocating mass, so one machine can deliver tens of thousands of horsepower smoothly; exhausting into a good condenser vacuum roughly doubles the output. It needs balanced rotors, close clearances and steady oil-fed bearings.
- Pitfalls:
  - Treating it as a big aeolipile or Branca's wheel; a single slow wheel wastes nearly all the energy
  - An unbalanced rotor at high speed shakes itself to pieces
  - Wet steam and carried-over water, which erode the blades
  - Coupling a ship's propeller directly; it spins too fast and cavitates (Turbinia needed nine propellers on three shafts)
- History: greece: 1st c. AD – Hero's aeolipile, a reaction turbine in principle only; islamic: 1551 – Taqi al-Din's steam-jet spit; europe: 1629 – Branca's impulse wheel on paper; 1883–1889 Gustaf de Laval's high-speed wheel and convergent-divergent nozzle; 1884 Charles Parsons's multi-stage turbine (about 7.5 kW at 18,000 rpm) driving a dynamo; 1897 Turbinia at the Spithead review, 34 knots; americas: 1896 – Curtis velocity-compounded turbine; 1903 5,000 kW units in Chicago power stations
- Read:
  - Charles A. Parsons, The Steam Turbine (Rede Lecture, 1911)
  - W. Garrett Scaife, From Galaxies to Turbines: Science, Technology and the Parsons Family (2000)
